name: Jade Zhang

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government, and we sell nothing. What you tell me is confidential. What is a usual day at the contact centre like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I take the complicated chats, especially when a customer has been passed around and is ready to leave. I am a team lead and one of the stronger agents, although my pay is low for this work. I use an AI drafting tool every day, then rewrite the answer so it fits the customer and the actual account.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is life like outside those shifts?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 27, have a two-year college diploma, and share a rented flat with my partner, Niko. We have no children. My savings would not cover a month of expenses, and there are few similar jobs nearby, so I keep a close eye on the roster even when I sound confident.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau: Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell people on my shift that the drafting tool stays a helper and we stay accountable for the answer. If AI mostly levels off, I would still show the newer agents how to catch a wrong promise before it reaches a customer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be glad the job remains, but I would not call our pay secure. My partner Niko has a steady wage, yet our rent and two sets of travel costs leave very little at month end. I am good at this job; I just cannot build savings on compliments.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would keep using the drafting tool and check each answer against the account notes. I would move a small set amount into savings on payday and ask about the next lead pay review. In the first year of this picture, I would stay on the difficult chat queue and keep our weekend spending down until we have a full month saved.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about my place on the team and uneasy about money. A small change in tools does not fix what my payslip says.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you say to Niko at home about a pay review?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say I am going to bring my case numbers and ask for a date, not just praise. Niko covers more of the rent already, and I do not want that to become our permanent arrangement.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which weekend spending would go?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We would cook at home more instead of buying dinner after my late shift. I would keep the bus pass, because getting to work is not optional.

I would make staff check **promises** against account notes.
think: My place feels **secure**, but my pay does not.
Niko covers more of our **rent** than I want.
do: Check each drafted **answer** against account notes.
Transfer a set amount into **savings** on payday.
Reduce bought **dinners** until we save a month.
S0.quote: I am good at this job; I just cannot build savings on compliments.
fieldNote: She uses AI **daily**, but claims responsibility for each answer.
Her main pressure is **pay**, even in the mild picture.
She wants a dated pay review rather than **praise** alone.

steps.text: Keep handling difficult customer chats and check AI drafts against account notes
Transfer a set amount from each payday into savings
Cook at home after late shifts until the couple saves one month of expenses

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption: Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team to learn the answer system while we can still shape how it works. We should record the cases it gets wrong and show management why a person must review an angry customer's account.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I can see the easy chats disappearing and the company cutting entry-level seats. I might be kept as a lead, but if fewer people need coaching my title loses its point. I do not want to wait for a layoff notice in a town with few centres.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I would ask to join the answer system pilot and collect examples of bad refunds or false promises. I would learn the tool's settings and the complaint rules on company time. During the first year as chats move to software, I would apply for a paid quality review role here, or for customer operations work in the next city if our hours shrink.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I am anxious, but I also want to get my hands on the system. Knowing exactly where it fails feels better than guessing from the staff room.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you tell newer agents that their jobs may go?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Yes, gently, with the evidence from the queue. I would show them the training options and tell them a course only helps if the company has a real paid place for them.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Can you afford to travel to the next city for work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if the wage covers the longer trip and my part of rent. I would compare the numbers before taking an interview day off.

I would show management its **wrong refunds** and false promises.
think: I expect easy **chats** to disappear and take some of our seats with them.
I worry a smaller team makes my **lead title** less secure.
do: Join the answer system **pilot** this week.
Apply for a **paid local quality role**, or next-city operations if hours shrink and wages cover travel and rent.
S1.quote: I do not want to wait for a layoff notice in a town with few centres.
fieldNote: She wants evidence from actual **refund cases**, not general warnings.
A next-city job must cover **travel** and rent.
She will encourage training only when a **paid place** exists.

steps.text: Join the answer system pilot and record wrong refunds this week

Apply for a posted paid local quality-review vacancy in the first year
Apply for next-city operations if hours shrink and wages cover travel and rent

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028: Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the floor that AGI by 2028 could take the calls before any training plan catches up. I would ask management to publish what human decisions it still expects and how those jobs will be paid.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my skill at calming customers might be copied on a screen within two years. Our contact centre is thinking work, so the robots around 2031 do not give my desk an extra three years. Niko's wage could carry part of our rent for a short time, but my share cannot simply vanish.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Today I would ask for the quality team's job criteria and a funded place in its next training round. I would save every spare amount after rent and ask Niko to agree which bills we could cut if my hours go. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2028, I would take a paid reviewer vacancy if one exists, and otherwise apply beyond the local centres before our reserve is gone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I am frightened by how short that runway is. I can move quickly, but I cannot invent a job opening.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What does that talk with Niko sound like?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell Niko the desk could be gone before our lease ends and ask us to price a cheaper flat. I would not ask my partner to promise to carry everything.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you leave your current job to study?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. I need its wage now, and a diploma with no paid vacancy at the end would drain our small reserve. I would ask for funded training while still on the roster.

say: I would ask for the remaining **human decisions** and wages.
I would ask for a plan before calls move by **2028**.
think: My customer skills could be copied within **two years**.
I cannot expect Niko to carry my **rent share** indefinitely on one wage.
do: Ask about funded **quality training** while still employed and save spare money after rent.
Plan possible **bill cuts** with Niko now.
Take a paid **reviewer vacancy** after 2028 if one exists; otherwise apply beyond local centres.
feel: I cannot create a **vacancy** by trying harder.
S2.quote: I can move quickly, but I cannot invent a job opening.
fieldNote: She understands robots arrive later but her **desk** faces AGI first.
Her speed is limited by **rent**, not willingness.
She refuses to turn Niko into a permanent **income plan**.

steps.text: Agree possible bill cuts and price a cheaper flat with Niko
Take a paid reviewer vacancy after 2028 if one exists
Save spare money after rent while still earning contact centre wages
Apply beyond local centres if no reviewer vacancy opens before savings run out

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031: Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell colleagues we have five years to make the company put names and wages on its new jobs. I would volunteer for the pilot work, then share what the tool can and cannot do with the team.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: By 2031 I could be in a different job, if I start now. I still expect our easy and difficult chats to be automated when full AGI comes, and a lead badge will not protect me. The extra years let me build evidence and savings before I choose where to move.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I would take the paid pilot shifts and ask to help audit customer outcomes. I would study account rules through a funded course and aim for three months of shared expenses in savings. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2031, I would take a paid audit or training role if there is a vacancy; if not, Niko and I would consider a move only after one of us has an offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the job but less trapped than in the fast picture. Five years gives me time to test whether the new role is real.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the audit team says you need another qualification?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the company to fund it or offer study time tied to a vacancy. I would not borrow for a certificate that may not lead to a wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why require an offer before moving?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Niko has a job here too. Moving two people with almost no savings on a guess would turn a work problem into a housing problem.

say: I would ask for **named jobs** and wages.
I would share findings from paid **pilot shifts** with the rest of the team.
think: I expect full AGI could take our **chats** by 2031.
The extra years help me build **evidence** and savings before choosing another job.
do: Move only after a **job offer** exists.
feel: Less **trapped** with time to test a route.
S3.quote: Moving two people with almost no savings on a guess would turn a work problem into a housing problem.
fieldNote: She wants a paid **audit path**, not an empty title.
Niko’s local job shapes the **move condition**.
Her savings target is three months of **shared expenses**.

steps.text: Take paid answer system pilot shifts and audit customer outcomes
Study account rules through employer funded training
Save toward three months of shared expenses

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036: Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my team ten years is enough to ask what customers still need and build skills for those tasks. We should insist on proper pay for the people who test the system and carry the complaints.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be 37 when AGI comes in 2036. I do not want to still be selling my time one chat at a time. I could build a route into customer operations or teaching new staff before then. Robots around 2039 do not change the order for our mostly screen-based work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would stay in the lead seat and propose a paid trial where I review AI answers and teach agents how to check them. If approved, I would run that trial on paid time. I would save toward a larger reserve and take a funded operations course only if it counts toward a role with a stated wage. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2036, I would apply for that operations role if it still exists, while Niko and I keep our housing costs manageable.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel fairly steady with a decade, though I would not coast. A clear path and savings would let me choose rather than scramble.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell a new agent starting next month?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would teach them the account rules and show them how to question a machine answer. I would also be honest that answering the simplest chats may not be a whole career.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you pay for that operations course yourself?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not with less than a month saved today. If the employer funds it or my savings grow enough and there is a stated wage at the end, I would consider it.

say: I would ask for proper **test pay** and complaint work.
I would teach new agents to question **machine answers**.
think: I can build an **operations path** before 2036.
I know **robots** come later than changes to our screens, so my plan starts earlier.
do: Propose a paid AI answer **review trial** now.
Take a funded **operations course** tied to wages.
S4.quote: I do not want to still be selling my time one chat at a time.
fieldNote: She wants to turn her daily AI use into **paid review work**.
Her course condition combines funding with a **stated wage**.
She thinks of 2036 as a **career deadline**, not a sudden surprise.

steps.text: Keep leading difficult customer chats while proposing a paid answer review trial

Build a larger shared savings reserve with Niko

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. A funded place in quality training, a list of real vacancies and pay rates, and a few months of warning before the roster changes would help. I could act on facts; I cannot budget on a promise.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who checks a wrong answer after the company cuts the people who know the account rules. The customer will still call back when a refund fails. Somebody should be paid to own that mistake.

headlineQuote: I could act on facts; I cannot budget on a promise.
portrait: Jade is a **27-year-old** contact centre lead with a two-year college diploma.
She is highly skilled and uses **AI daily**, but her pay is low and savings cover less than a month.
She shares rent with **Niko**, whose wage cannot replace hers for long.
She moves early toward **paid quality work**, and tests each option against wages and real vacancies.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could automate her chats before she secures another paid role.
whatWouldHelp: **Funded training**, named vacancies with pay rates and warning before roster cuts would help.
